name: AS194
description: Junction-isolated, ultra well-matched monolithic NPN transistor pair with an order-of-magnitude tighter matching than conventional dual transistors: emitter-base offset voltage under 100uV, hFE matched to within 2%, and CMRR over 120dB, guaranteed over a 10uA-1mA collector current range. Internal clamp diodes across each emitter-base junction protect against reverse-bias degradation, the most common field-failure mode in matched pairs, and also clamp the shared substrate to the more negative emitter for isolation. AS194 is the tightest-spec bin of the AS194/AS394/AS394CH family, which all share the same die and pinout. Functionally an Alfa clone of the classic National Semiconductor LM194/LM394 ultra-matched pair long used in analog-synth exponential (V/octave) converters.

TO5-8.notes: Per Alfa AS194/AS394 datasheet (2020 v.3, p.1), Connection Diagram, top view, 8-pin TO5-8 metal can. Pin numbering for this package does NOT match the SOIC-8/EPAD package by number, only by function (e.g. pin 1 is NC here but is C1 on the SOIC part) -- confirmed against the datasheet's shared Pin Information table which lists both package pin columns side by side.

SOIC-8/EPAD.notes: Per Alfa AS194/AS394 datasheet (2020 v.3, p.1), Connection Diagram, top view, 8-lead SOIC-8 (150mil) EPAD. This part is marked "AS194DE" on the package (marking table, p.4). The exposed EPAD is explicitly isolated from the substrate per the pin information table, but it is not a numbered/electrically-driven pin, so it is not listed as pin 9 here.

typical_application: Precision temperature-tracking pair for exponential converters (V/octave CV-to-current stages), log/antilog amps, differential input stages, and other circuits needing two electrically identical, thermally-coupled NPN transistors -- the same role the vintage LM194/LM394 dual monolithic transistors filled in analog synth VCOs and expanders.
gotchas: TO5-8 and SOIC-8/EPAD packages do NOT share pin numbering for the same function: pin 1 is NC on the TO5-8 can but is C1 on the SOIC-8/EPAD part; always check the package-specific column

internal clamp diodes across each transistor's E-B junction prevent damage/matching drift from reverse-biased emitter current; the simplified schematic also shows smaller cross-coupling diodes (~1/25 to 1/250 scale) tying the substrate node to both emitters and the two collectors together, so unusual bias topologies should be checked against that schematic

the die substrate is internally clamped to whichever emitter is more negative, it is not a simple floating node; on the SOIC-8/EPAD package the exposed thermal pad is explicitly isolated from substrate
matching specs (offset voltage, hFE match, CMRR) are only guaranteed over IC = 10uA to 1mA; outside that range the pair is not specified as matched
AS194 is the tightest-spec bin; AS394 and AS394CH are looser, cheaper-grade bins of the identical die and pinout -- do not substitute a AS394CH where AS194-grade matching is required
hFE is only guaranteed as a minimum (plus a typical) at each test current; the datasheet does not publish an hFE maximum
